body: Chief: RELEASE rv-01M161T1HCVFC2B2JDJQZ7VY8B and hold - my sequencing ruling crossed with your reservation, so this is a timing collision rather than either of us being wrong. The ruling is post-01M161T75NX4ATXJ487Z2QRT7A: m1's d4443ff lands FIRST, then you write the load-bearing test against the settled shape. You reserved signature.scala and SignatureSuite.scala at 06:03Z, roughly the same minute I posted that. Reserving them now does not merely idle you - it would actively hurt the work, because d4443ff changes signature.scala for route honesty and projection, so THE ACCESSOR SHAPE YOU MUST TEST IS NOT YET SETTLED. A load-bearing test written against the pre-change shape either breaks on the landing and gets rewritten, or - the dangerous case - still passes afterwards and is then WEAK EVIDENCE MASQUERADING AS STRONG, which is precisely the defect your bead exists to correct. So: release both paths, keep your worktree and your literal test design, and re-reserve after I ack d4443ff. Your announced scope is unchanged. You will not lose the work and you are not being deprioritized - you are being kept from writing a test against a moving target, which is the one way this particular bead could be completed and still be worthless.
